title: 5-Axis Post Processing + Output Generation + Verification
description: Build the FiveAxisPostEngine for complete 5-axis post processing (RTCP/TCPC, singularity management, rotary axis limits, inverse time feed, linearization). Wire Phase 6 (output generation) — controller-specific G-code generation through ControllerDialectEngine, probe routines, setup sheets, analytics reports, cycle time estimation, and digital twin snapshots. Build PostProcessorVerificationEngine for output validation — grammar checking, travel limit verification, backplot reconstruction.

units.title: FiveAxisPostEngine — RTCP/TCPC + Rotary axis management + Inverse time feed
steps: Create FiveAxisPostEngine.ts (~1500 lines)
RTCP/TCPC output per controller:
Fanuc: G43.4 (Type 1) / G43.5 (Type 2) with H offset
Siemens: TRAORI / TRAFOOF, CYCLE800 for swivel planes
Heidenhain: FUNCTION TCPM with axis selection (AXIS POS STAY/PATHCTRL)
Haas: G234 (DWO — Dynamic Work Offset)
Mazak: G43.4 with pivot point definition
Okuma: G43.4/G43.5 variant + coordinate rotation
Pivot point / gauge length handling per machine kinematics
Rotary axis management:
Detect axis wrapping requirements (0-360, ±180, ±99999, hard stops)
Insert axis unwind moves when approaching limits
Handle axis flip at singularity (B=0 for head-head: A jumps 180°)
Shortest path rotation selection (CW vs CCW)
Inverse time feed (G93) calculation:
For 5-axis simultaneous: F = 1/time_per_block (minutes)
Combined linear + rotary distance → equivalent feed rate
Handle transition between G93 (inverse time) and G94 (feed per minute)
Linearization with tolerance control:
Break long 5-axis moves into linear segments within tolerance
User-configurable linearization tolerance (default 0.01mm)
Minimize number of segments while maintaining tolerance (binary search)
Coordinate system rotation:
G68.2 (Fanuc tilted work plane)
CYCLE800 (Siemens swivel)
Plane Spatial (Heidenhain)
G68 (Mazak coordinate rotation)
exit_conditions: 5-axis program with TCPC produces correct G-code for Fanuc, Siemens, Heidenhain
Rotary axis unwind inserted before limit violation
Inverse time feed calculated correctly for combined linear+rotary moves
Linearization tolerance maintained within user specification
Singularity detection flags and manages pole regions
30+ tests covering 5-axis scenarios

units.title: Stage 6.1-6.2 — G-code generation through ControllerDialectEngine + Controller parameter blocks
steps: Wire ControllerDialectEngine (from PP-MS3) as the G-code code generator
For each ToolpathBlock → generate controller-specific G-code line using dialect rules
Safe start block: controller-specific initialization (G90 G21 G17 G40 G80 order per dialect)
Tool change sequence: per machine type (vertical spindle, horizontal, turret, ATC)
Canned cycle generation: translate drill/tap/bore operations to controller-specific cycles
Arc output: IJK vs R format per controller dialect
Sub-program generation: if repeated geometry, extract to sub-program per controller convention
Controller parameter blocks: insert at program start and per-operation as needed
Look-ahead depth setting (where configurable)
Smoothing mode / tolerance setting
HSC mode activation
TCPC/RTCP activation for 5-axis
Program end: controller-specific (M30, M2, END PGM, M99 for sub-program)
Line numbering: per controller convention (N10 N20... or N1 N2... or no numbers)
exit_conditions: Same toolpath produces valid G-code for all 15 controller dialects
Canned cycles translated correctly (G81 ↔ CYCLE81 ↔ BORE1)
Controller parameter blocks appropriate for operation type
Program structure (header, tool changes, operations, end) follows controller conventions

units.title: Stage 6.3-6.5 — Probe routines + Setup sheet + Analytics report
steps: Wire ProbeRoutineGeneratorEngine: insert probe routines at strategic points
WCS setup: probe reference surfaces before first cut
In-process inspection: probe critical features after finishing (optional, user-configurable)
Tool measurement: tool length/diameter measurement before first use (G37/G38 or controller-specific)
Wire SetupSheetFromGCodeEngine: generate complete setup sheet from pipeline data
Tool list with: tool number, description, holder, gauge length, RPM range, feed range, coolant type
Work holding description, WCS datum location, clamping force requirements
Safety notes from playbook and safety analysis
Estimated cycle time, stock material, tolerance callouts
Generate analytics report:
Per-operation: force range (with CI), power range, temperature range, MRR, tool wear prediction
Per-tool: estimated tool life consumed, remaining life, cost per part
Overall: total cycle time, cutting time vs non-cutting, energy estimate, cost estimate
Optimization impact: time saved vs constant S/F, force reduction, tool life improvement
exit_conditions: Probe routines generated for controller-specific syntax
Setup sheet contains all necessary info for operator (no gaps)
Analytics report shows per-operation and overall metrics
Optimization impact quantified as % improvement over constant S/F baseline

units.title: Stage 6.6-6.7 — Cycle time estimation + Digital twin snapshot
steps: Wire CycleTimeEstimatorEngine: calculate realistic cycle time using machine motion model
Not just distance/feed — account for acceleration, deceleration, servo settling, tool change time
Use MotionDynamicsProfileEngine achievable feeds (not commanded feeds) for realistic estimate
Breakdown: cutting time, rapid time, tool change time, probe time, dwell time
Wire digital twin snapshot: save predicted state for post-run comparison
Snapshot includes: predicted forces per block, temperatures, wear state, dimensional predictions
Format for future comparison with actual monitoring data (when available)
This enables the Bayesian adaptive learning loop — compare predicted vs actual, update priors
exit_conditions: Cycle time estimate within 10% of actual for well-characterized machines
Time breakdown shows cutting vs non-cutting ratio
Digital twin snapshot serializable and loadable
Snapshot format compatible with DigitalTwinSyncEngine

units.title: PostProcessorVerificationEngine — Grammar + Travel limits + Backplot
steps: Create PostProcessorVerificationEngine.ts (~1000 lines)
Controller grammar validation:
Parse generated G-code against controller-specific grammar rules
Check: valid G/M codes for controller, correct argument format, block structure
Check: no deprecated codes, no unsupported features for controller version
Check: mandatory codes present (e.g., T before M6, S before M3)
Travel limit verification:
Simulate all moves and verify within machine work volume (X/Y/Z/A/B/C limits)
Check rapids for potential crash zones (above stock, avoid fixtures if geometry provided)
Verify Z clearance plane is safe
Feed/speed sanity check:
All S values within machine RPM range
All F values within machine axis feed rate limits
No zero or negative feeds on cutting moves
Sequence validation:
Program number format correct
Tool calls in valid order
Coolant on before cut, off before tool change
Work offset set before cutting
Backplot reconstruction:
Parse output G-code back to XYZ points
Verify reconstructed path matches original toolpath within tolerance
Detect any path deviations introduced by smoothing or linearization
exit_conditions: Grammar validation catches invalid G/M codes per controller
Travel limit check catches out-of-envelope moves
Backplot reconstruction matches original within 0.001mm
Validation report returned with pass/fail per check category
20+ tests covering validation scenarios
